notes: Buy a SUBE card (from kiosks). The metro (Subte) and buses (colectivo) are cheap, and Uber and Cabify are safe. Ezeiza is 1 hour away; Aeroparque is in the city.
NOTE: June to September is winter in Argentina (8-15°C, grey), so plan indoor stops: museums, cafés, tango. The July winter holiday is crowded, and Colonia is windy.

ARS inflation means prices change fast (ASSUMPTION: mid-2026). The 'dólar MEP' rate applied automatically to card payments is good, while Western Union is for cash. The new USD 100 series is in circulation.
Parrilla 30,000-60,000 ARS, empanada 2,000 ARS, coffee and medialuna 5,000 ARS, tango show 90,000+ ARS. Tip 10% in cash; dinner starts after 21:00.
Watch out for pickpockets: outside Caminito's main street and at the Retiro bus terminal. Don't show your phone in the street. Bring your passport for Colonia.
Try shared mate, dulce de leche, alfajor (Havanna) and malbec; there is a Recoleta feria on Sundays.

stops.name: Plaza de Mayo
stops.tips: Casa Rosada (the pink palace, free tours at weekends), the Cathedral (Pope Francis's former church), Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo on Thursdays at 15:30.

stops.name: Café Tortoni
stops.tips: A café since 1858; order churros and hot chocolate. Expect a queue. On Avenida de Mayo.

stops.name: San Telmo Market
stops.tips: A market since 1897 with choripán and empanada stalls and antique dealers. On Sundays the Defensa street feria stretches for 10 blocks.

stops.name: Plaza Dorrego
stops.tips: Street tango (Sundays) and antique shops.

stops.name: El Zanjón de Granados
stops.tips: 1730 tunnels beneath a restored mansion; visit by guided tour.

backups.name: La Brigada San Telmo
backups.tips: A parrilla with football decor; the meat is so tender it is cut with a spoon.

backups.name: Museo Histórico Nacional
backups.tips: National history in Parque Lezama; free. Visit instead of Zanjón.

stops.name: Recoleta Cemetery
stops.tips: A city of marble mausoleums with Evita's grave (Duarte) and plenty of cats. Free, but since 2025 foreigners pay 14,000 ARS for a ticket.

stops.name: Floralis Genérica
stops.tips: A giant steel flower that opens and closes with the sun, in Plaza Naciones Unidas.

stops.name: MALBA
stops.tips: Latin American art, including Frida Kahlo and Berni. Discounted on Wednesdays.

stops.name: Bosques de Palermo & Rosedal
stops.tips: A rose garden and lakes; hire a rowing boat or a bike.

stops.name: Don Julio
stops.tips: Billed as the world's best steakhouse. Without a reservation, join the queue at 18:45 (champagne is served while you wait). Order the bife de chorizo and a malbec.

backups.name: El Preferido de Palermo
backups.tips: Don Julio's pink sibling, serving milanesa and tapas.

backups.name: Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes
backups.tips: Free; Rodin and Monet, near Recoleta.

stops.name: Caminito
stops.tips: Colourful tin houses and street tango. Go in daylight and stay on the main streets.

stops.name: La Bombonera Boca Juniors
stops.tips: Stadium and museum tour; a shrine to Maradona.

stops.name: El Obrero La Boca
stops.tips: A workers' canteen from 1954 serving milanesa and tortilla. Bono has eaten here.

stops.name: Puente de la Mujer
stops.tips: Calatrava's bridge and the old docks, with the Fragata Sarmiento ship.

stops.name: Reserva Ecológica Costanera Sur
stops.tips: A nature reserve on the Rio de la Plata shore. Come for sunset; choripán stands are outside.

backups.name: Usina del Arte
backups.tips: Concert hall and gallery in a former power station; in La Boca, free.

stops.name: Tren de la Costa Tigre
stops.tips: The Mitre train from Retiro takes 1 hour (or take the scenic Tren de la Costa) to the Tigre station.

stops.name: Puerto de Frutos
stops.tips: A market at the old fruit port selling wicker, woodwork and mate gourds.

stops.name: Tigre Delta Boat Tour
stops.tips: Paraná delta channels, stilt houses and market boats. The Interisleña public boat is cheap.

stops.name: Museo de Arte Tigre
stops.tips: The 1912 Tigre Club palace, a Belle Époque building on the riverbank.

stops.name: María Luján Tigre
stops.tips: A riverside parrilla with asado and views.

backups.name: Museo del Mate
backups.tips: A mate museum with tastings, in Tigre.

backups.name: Almacén de Ramos Generales Tigre
backups.tips: A former general store turned restaurant; try the picada (sharing platter).

stops.name: Buquebus Colonia Feribotu
stops.tips: Ferry crossing of 1 hour 15 minutes (bring your passport; about 70,000 ARS return online) to Uruguay.

stops.name: Barrio Histórico Colonia
stops.tips: A UNESCO-listed Portuguese-Spanish town with the Calle de los Suspiros and the Portuguese gate.

stops.name: Faro de Colonia
stops.tips: A lighthouse from 1857 with views over the Rio de la Plata (pay in UYU cash).

stops.name: Charco Bistró Colonia
stops.tips: A riverside bistro; try the chivito (Uruguayan steak sandwich). Pay in UYU or USD.

stops.name: Rambla & Plaza Mayor
stops.tips: A coastal road with classic cars. Take the ferry back between 17:00 and 19:00, before sunset.

backups.name: Museo Portugués Colonia
backups.tips: A museum of the Portuguese period; visit instead of the lighthouse.

backups.name: El Buen Suspiro Colonia
backups.tips: Wine and picada (sharing platter) on Calle de los Suspiros.

stops.name: Plaza Serrano Palermo Soho
stops.tips: Boutiques and murals; a design market at weekends.

stops.name: La Cabrera Palermo
stops.tips: Parrilla with 15 small side dishes; 40% off during happy hour, 12:00-13:30.

stops.name: Museo Evita
stops.tips: Evita's clothes and life story, in a Palermo mansion.

stops.name: El Ateneo Grand Splendid
stops.tips: A bookshop in a former theatre, often called the most beautiful in the world. On Santa Fe.

stops.name: Tango Show El Viejo Almacén
stops.tips: San Telmo's most traditional tango show, with a dinner package. A milonga (La Viruta) is a cheaper alternative.

backups.name: La Viruta Milonga
backups.tips: A milonga where locals dance; lesson plus night out.

backups.name: Sarkis Palermo
backups.tips: Armenian meze; a good alternative to a parrilla. Expect a queue.

days.theme: Teatro Colón and a gentle farewell

stops.name: Teatro Colón
stops.tips: An opera house with some of the world's best acoustics. English tours run every hour; see the golden hall.

stops.name: Obelisco & Avenida 9 de Julio
stops.tips: The world's widest avenue and its obelisk, the symbol of Buenos Aires.

stops.name: Confitería La Ideal
stops.tips: A café restored from 1912; have medialunas (small croissants) and a café con leche as a farewell.

stops.name: Galerías Pacífico
stops.tips: A shopping centre with a frescoed dome; buy leather souvenirs (Calle Florida).

stops.name: Ezeiza Airport Tienda León
stops.tips: Bus or taxi takes 1 hour; farewell.

backups.name: Museo de Arte Decorativo
backups.tips: The Errázuriz palace; visit instead of the Colón.

backups.name: Las Violetas Almagro
backups.tips: A stained-glass café from 1884; try the medialunas (small croissants).
